title: Manifold Absolute Pressure (MAP) Circuit
problem: The Engine Control Unit (ECU) has detected a general malfunction in the Manifold Absolute Pressure sensor circuit, indicating an electrical fault or out-of-range signal.
symptoms: Poor engine performance; Reduced fuel efficiency; Check Engine Light (CEL) illuminated
actions: Check MAP sensor wiring for damage; Clean MAP sensor port; Test MAP sensor output
location: Located on the intake manifold

title: MAP Sensor Circuit Low Input
problem: The MAP sensor is sending a voltage signal to the ECU that is lower than expected, usually indicating a short circuit or sensor failure.
symptoms: Rough idle; Engine stall; Reduced power
actions: Inspect MAP sensor wiring for shorts; Verify sensor voltage with a multimeter; Replace MAP sensor
location: Located on the intake manifold

title: MAP Sensor Circuit High Input
problem: The MAP sensor is sending a voltage signal to the ECU that is higher than expected, suggesting an open circuit, short to voltage, or sensor failure.
symptoms: Hesitation on acceleration; Poor fuel economy; CEL illuminated
actions: Check MAP sensor wiring for opens or shorts to power; Test sensor resistance; Replace MAP sensor
location: Located on the intake manifold

title: Intake Air Temperature (IAT) Sensor High Input
problem: The IAT sensor is reporting an abnormally high temperature to the ECU, often due to an open circuit or faulty sensor, leading to incorrect fuel mixture calculations.
symptoms: Hard starting in cold weather; Poor fuel economy; Engine running rich
actions: Inspect IAT sensor wiring for open circuits; Test sensor resistance at various temperatures; Replace IAT sensor
location: Located in the airbox or intake tract.

title: Engine Coolant Temperature (ECT) Sensor High Input
problem: The ECT sensor is sending an abnormally high temperature signal to the ECU, indicating an open circuit, short to voltage, or sensor failure.
symptoms: Overheating indications without actual overheat; Poor cold start; Incorrect fan operation
actions: Check ECT sensor wiring for opens or shorts to power; Test sensor resistance; Replace ECT sensor
location: Located on the cylinder head or coolant passage.

title: Throttle Position Sensor (TPS) A Low Input
problem: The primary Throttle Position Sensor (TPS A) is sending a voltage signal lower than the acceptable range, potentially due to a short circuit or sensor fault, affecting throttle response.
symptoms: Engine power loss; Erratic idle; Throttle unresponsive
actions: Inspect TPS wiring for shorts; Calibrate TPS if adjustable; Replace TPS sensor
location: Attached to the throttle body.

title: Throttle Position Sensor (TPS) A High Input
problem: The primary Throttle Position Sensor (TPS A) is sending a voltage signal higher than the acceptable range, often due to an open circuit or sensor fault, leading to unpredictable throttle behavior.
symptoms: High idle; Unintended acceleration; CEL illuminated
actions: Check TPS wiring for opens or shorts to power; Verify TPS voltage range; Replace TPS sensor
location: Attached to the throttle body.

title: O2 Sensor Circuit Malfunction (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
problem: The ECU has detected an electrical fault in the pre-catalyst oxygen sensor circuit, meaning the sensor is not providing valid data, impacting fuel trim adjustments.
symptoms: Increased fuel consumption; Poor engine performance; CEL illuminated
actions: Inspect O2 sensor wiring for damage; Check O2 sensor connector; Replace O2 sensor
location: Located in the exhaust header

title: O2 Sensor Heater Circuit Malfunction (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
problem: The heater element within the pre-catalyst oxygen sensor is not functioning correctly, preventing the sensor from reaching operating temperature quickly, affecting emissions and fuel control.
symptoms: Delayed closed-loop operation; Higher emissions; CEL illuminated
actions: Check O2 sensor heater fuse; Test O2 sensor heater resistance; Replace O2 sensor
location: Located in the exhaust header

title: System Too Lean (Bank 1)
problem: The ECU detects that the engine is running with too much air or not enough fuel for the commanded conditions, leading to an overly lean air-fuel mixture.
symptoms: Rough idle; Loss of power; Engine hesitation
actions: Check for vacuum leaks in intake system; Inspect fuel pressure and injectors; Clean or replace mass air flow (MAF) sensor (if applicable)
location: Engine compartment

title: System Too Rich (Bank 1)
problem: The ECU detects that the engine is running with too much fuel or not enough air, resulting in an overly rich air-fuel mixture.
symptoms: Poor fuel economy; Black smoke from exhaust; Strong fuel odor
actions: Check fuel pressure regulator; Inspect fuel injectors for leaks; Test O2 sensor and ECT sensor
location: Engine compartment

title: Injector Circuit/Open - Cylinder 1
problem: The ECU has detected an open circuit or electrical malfunction in the fuel injector circuit for cylinder 1, meaning the injector is not firing correctly or at all.
symptoms: Engine misfire; Rough running; Loss of power
actions: Check injector wiring for damage; Test injector resistance; Replace fuel injector
location: Located in the intake manifold for Cylinder 1.

title: Injector Circuit/Open - Cylinder 2
problem: The ECU has detected an open circuit or electrical malfunction in the fuel injector circuit for cylinder 2, meaning the injector is not firing correctly or at all.
symptoms: Engine misfire; Rough running; Loss of power
actions: Check injector wiring for damage; Test injector resistance; Replace fuel injector
location: Located in the intake manifold for Cylinder 2 (for twin-cylinder models).

title: Injector Circuit Low - Cylinder 1
problem: The voltage in the fuel injector circuit for cylinder 1 is lower than specified, indicating a short to ground or faulty injector driver.
symptoms: Engine misfire; Reduced power; Increased emissions
actions: Inspect injector wiring for shorts to ground; Check ECU injector driver; Replace fuel injector
location: Located in the intake manifold for Cylinder 1.

title: Injector Circuit Low - Cylinder 2
problem: The voltage in the fuel injector circuit for cylinder 2 is lower than specified, indicating a short to ground or faulty injector driver.
symptoms: Engine misfire; Reduced power; Increased emissions
actions: Inspect injector wiring for shorts to ground; Check ECU injector driver; Replace fuel injector
location: Located in the intake manifold for Cylinder 2 (for twin-cylinder models).

title: Crankshaft Position Sensor A Circuit
problem: The ECU is not receiving a valid signal from the crankshaft position sensor, which is essential for engine timing and RPM, often causing a no-start condition.
symptoms: No start; Engine cranking but not firing; Erratic RPM readings
actions: Check CKP sensor wiring for damage; Test CKP sensor resistance; Replace CKP sensor
location: Located near the crankshaft

title: Camshaft Position Sensor A Circuit
problem: The ECU is not receiving a valid signal from the camshaft position sensor, affecting valve timing and ignition sync, potentially causing starting issues or poor performance.
symptoms: Hard starting; Engine stalls; Reduced engine power
actions: Check CMP sensor wiring for damage; Test CMP sensor resistance; Replace CMP sensor
location: Located near the camshaft

title: Ignition Coil A Primary/Secondary Circuit (Cylinder 1)
problem: The ECU has detected an electrical fault in the primary or secondary circuit of the ignition coil for cylinder 1, leading to a lack of spark.
symptoms: Engine misfire; Rough idle; Loss of power
actions: Inspect coil wiring for damage; Test ignition coil resistance; Replace ignition coil
location: Located on top of the spark plug for Cylinder 1.

title: Ignition Coil B Primary/Secondary Circuit (Cylinder 2)
problem: The ECU has detected an electrical fault in the primary or secondary circuit of the ignition coil for cylinder 2, leading to a lack of spark.
symptoms: Engine misfire; Rough idle; Loss of power
actions: Inspect coil wiring for damage; Test ignition coil resistance; Replace ignition coil
location: Located on top of the spark plug for Cylinder 2 (for twin-cylinder models).

title: EVAP Purge Control Valve Circuit
problem: An electrical malfunction has been detected in the circuit controlling the EVAP (Evaporative Emission Control System) purge valve, which manages fuel vapor flow.
symptoms: Increased emissions; Poor fuel economy; CEL illuminated
actions: Check EVAP purge valve wiring; Test purge valve solenoid; Replace EVAP purge valve
location: Mounted on or near the intake manifold

title: Vehicle Speed Sensor A Malfunction
problem: The ECU is not receiving a valid signal from the vehicle speed sensor, impacting speedometer, cruise control, and shifting (if applicable).
symptoms: Inaccurate speedometer; Cruise control inoperative; Incorrect gear shifting (if applicable)
actions: Inspect VSS wiring for damage; Clean VSS sensor; Replace VSS sensor
location: Typically located on the transmission output shaft or wheel hub.

title: Idle Control System RPM Malfunction
problem: The engine's idle speed is not being controlled correctly by the ECU, potentially due to a faulty IAC valve or a dirty/damaged throttle body.
symptoms: High idle; Low idle; Engine stalls at idle
actions: Clean throttle body and IAC passage; Inspect IAC valve wiring; Replace IAC valve or throttle body
location: Part of the throttle body assembly.

title: System Voltage Malfunction
problem: The ECU has detected an abnormal voltage reading from the vehicle's electrical system, indicating a general problem with power supply.
symptoms: Dim lights; Electrical component malfunction; Hard starting
actions: Check battery terminals and charge; Test alternator output; Inspect main fuses
location: Battery compartment

title: System Voltage Low
problem: The ECU detects that the system voltage is consistently below the normal operating range, often pointing to a weak battery or charging system issue.
symptoms: Engine cranking slowly; Dim headlights; Electronic components failing
actions: Check battery voltage and condition; Inspect alternator output; Test voltage regulator
location: Battery compartment

title: System Voltage High
problem: The ECU detects that the system voltage is consistently above the normal operating range, indicating a potential overcharging issue, which can damage electronics.
symptoms: Bulbs burning out frequently; Electronics behaving erratically; Battery swelling
actions: Test voltage regulator output; Inspect alternator; Check for wiring shorts to power
location: Battery compartment

title: Internal Control Module Memory Check Sum Error
problem: An internal error has occurred within the ECU's memory, indicating a potential corruption of its software or data, often requiring ECU replacement.
symptoms: No start; Engine running erratically; Multiple unrelated fault codes
actions: Attempt ECU reflash (if possible); Check ECU power/ground; Replace ECU
location: Under the seat or in the fairing

title: Internal Control Module RAM Error
problem: An error has been detected in the ECU's Random Access Memory (RAM), which stores temporary data, suggesting an internal hardware fault.
symptoms: Engine stalling; Intermittent starting; Unpredictable engine behavior
actions: Check ECU power and ground connections; Inspect for moisture intrusion in ECU; Replace ECU
location: Under the seat or in the fairing

title: Internal Control Module ROM Error
problem: An error has been detected in the ECU's Read Only Memory (ROM), where the main operating program is stored, indicating a critical internal hardware or software fault.
symptoms: No start; Engine fails to run; Complete loss of engine control
actions: Check ECU power and ground; Attempt ECU reflash if applicable; Replace ECU
location: Under the seat or in the fairing

title: MIL Control Circuit Malfunction
problem: The ECU has detected a fault in the circuit that controls the Malfunction Indicator Lamp (Check Engine Light) on the dashboard.
symptoms: Check Engine Light not illuminating; Check Engine Light constantly on (without other codes); Failure to pass inspection
actions: Check MIL bulb/LED; Inspect MIL control circuit wiring; Test instrument cluster
location: Instrument cluster on the dashboard.

title: Fuel Pump Relay Fault
problem: The KTM ECU detects an open or short in the fuel pump relay circuit, preventing the fuel pump from operating or operating intermittently.
symptoms: Engine no-start; Engine stalling; Fuel pump not priming
actions: Check fuel pump relay fuse; Test fuel pump relay for clicks; Inspect wiring to fuel pump relay
location: Typically located in the fuse box or near the battery.

title: Engine Temperature Sensor Fault
problem: The KTM ECU detects an invalid signal from the engine temperature sensor, leading to incorrect fuel maps and cooling fan operation.
symptoms: Engine running rich/lean; Cooling fan running constantly or not at all; Hard starting
actions: Check ECT sensor wiring; Test ECT sensor resistance; Replace ECT sensor
location: Located on the cylinder head or coolant passage.

title: Clutch Switch Fault
problem: The KTM ECU detects an open or short in the clutch switch circuit, which is used for starting interlocks and quickshifter functionality.
symptoms: Engine won't start in gear; Quickshifter not working; Cruise control issues
actions: Inspect clutch switch wiring; Adjust clutch lever free play; Replace clutch switch
location: Mounted on the clutch lever assembly.

title: Sidestand Switch Fault
problem: The KTM ECU detects an open or short in the sidestand switch circuit, which is a safety interlock to prevent riding with the sidestand down.
symptoms: Engine stalls when in gear; Engine won't start; Difficult shifting
actions: Inspect sidestand switch wiring for damage; Clean sidestand switch; Replace sidestand switch
location: Mounted on the sidestand assembly.

title: Front Wheel Speed Sensor Malfunction
problem: The ABS control module is not receiving a valid speed signal from the front wheel speed sensor, affecting ABS and potentially traction control.
symptoms: ABS light on; Traction control light on; Loss of ABS function
actions: Inspect sensor wiring for damage; Clean sensor and tone ring; Replace front wheel speed sensor
location: Located on the front wheel axle/fork

title: Rear Wheel Speed Sensor Malfunction
problem: The ABS control module is not receiving a valid speed signal from the rear wheel speed sensor, affecting ABS and potentially traction control.
symptoms: ABS light on; Traction control light on; Loss of ABS function
actions: Inspect sensor wiring for damage; Clean sensor and tone ring; Replace rear wheel speed sensor
location: Located on the rear wheel axle/swingarm

title: ABS Pump Motor Fault
problem: The ABS control module has detected an internal fault with its pump motor, which is responsible for modulating brake pressure during ABS activation.
symptoms: ABS light on; Brake pedal pulsation (false); Complete loss of ABS function

location: Part of the throttle body assembly.

location: Engine control system (ECU and throttle body).

symptoms: Engine limp mode; Unresponsive throttle; CEL illuminated

location: Attached to the throttle body

title: Throttle Position Sensor E Circuit Low Input
